"═══ SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO ═══

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección \"SOP omgithub\" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final \"── FIN DEL SOP ──\" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: \"Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md\".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

2.1 CENSO
    Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero.
    Agrupar linajes de prompts idénticos/repetidos.
    Cota forense: leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes.
    >7 días o fuera de cota → compostar SIN leer.

2.2 FORENSIS (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
    a) Tres fuentes, en orden de autoridad:
       1. Diff de código huérfano → qué hizo.
       2. HANDOFF.md del repo → qué se proponía.
       3. Thread del issue (último Work State/Next Move) → por qué murió.
       Reconciliar en UNA línea: \"causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente\".
    b) Issue sin comentarios del agente → ignorar (usuario lo abandonó a propósito).

2.3 COMPOST (por unidad)
    Rescate a main vía branch temporal:
       git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main
       merge checkpoints/N → si limpio y build verde:
          push FF tmp-main:main (+ tag save-NNN si es hito)
       si no: tag graveyard-checkpoints-N + mención en epitafio.
    Luego borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main, o sin código).
    Volver a tu branch; el sync [3.2] absorberá el main compostado.

2.4 SEPULTURA (mantenimiento de issues)
    Cerrar el issue con comment-epitafio:
    \"⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W\"
    Sin permiso para cerrar → Comment \"⚰ CERRABLE: ...\" y listar en reporte.

2.5 HIGIENE POST-FUNERAL
    Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máx 1 esperando humano).
    Reportar conteo final en el epitafio.

[3] BOOT
3.1 Leer: AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.
3.2 Sync preciso: HEAD ancestro de origin/main → reset --hard origin/main.
    Divergidas → merge limpio + rebuild; conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte.
3.3 Triage huérfano: si origin/main..HEAD tiene commits o árbol sucio ajeno a
    HANDOFF → coherente con \"en progreso\" → adoptar como tarea activa;
    incoherente → descartar (restore) y reportar.
3.4 Gate baseline: build (+tests si existen). Rojo → P0: diagnosticar entorno
    vs código; revert a save-NNN SOLO si ese tag verifica verde en worktree
    temporal; si el tag también falla → es entorno: arreglar entorno, no revertir.
3.5 Sin tags save-* → git tag save-000 @COMMENT_BODY@@COMMENT_BODY@ push.

[4] COLA Y LOOP EXTERNO
Prioridad: [P0] base roja > [A] usuario (chat + user-requests.md) >
[B] roadmap > [C] mantenimiento > [D] green.
Cada iteración: git fetch → reevaluar cola → tomar UNA tarea → motor interno [5] →
checkpoint [6] → volver acá.

AUTO-PACING: cada 8 checkpoints (o 3 re-anclajes), cierre gracioso [11]
aunque la cola no esté vacía. Muerte limpia > muerte infligida.

Cola vacía → HANDOFF + checkpoint final + reporte + pausa.

[5] MOTOR RALPH INTERNO (por tarea)
PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3-6 líneas en HANDOFF \"en progreso\".
ACT: edición mínima que cumple la tarea; solo archivos del scope.
VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea: \"¿qué podría romper esto?\". Si la respuesta es seria →
  agregar test o guarda antes de cerrar.
FIX: VERIFY fallido → diagnosticar → corregir → re-VERIFY (máx 3 rondas).
DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo
  commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.

Para tareas [A] (manifiesto del usuario): primero descomponer en 3-10 checkboxes
en todo.md o roadmap; luego ejecutarlas de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.

DESCARTE: 3 rondas sin éxito → revertir archivos de la tarea, todo.md con
  motivo e intentos, siguiente tarea.

[6] CHECKPOINTS
6.1 DONE con build verde → git push origin HEAD:main (fast-forward). Nunca force.
6.2 Rechazo \"non-fast-forward\" → fetch + merge limpio + rebuild → push;
    conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte; el loop SIGUE con [C]/[D] sin
    checkpointear reintentando el sync cada iteración; pausa total recién
    tras 3 iteraciones con el mismo conflicto.
6.3 Rechazo \"403/permission\" → no reintentar: reportar una vez \"falta permiso
    de push a main\" y seguir sin checkpoint hasta resolución humana.
6.4 Tag save-NNN solo con VERIFY aprobado (hito visible).
6.5 Todo checkpoint es punto de muerte segura.

[7] LIBROS
• HANDOFF.md: reescribir SOLO en pausa, cierre y re-anclaje (cada 5 tareas).
• todo.md: descartadas/bloqueadas con intentos (máx 3 de por vida → \"requiere humano\").
• user-requests.md: inbox externo; tachar al completar.
• roadmap/*.md: autogestionado con checkboxes; archivo completo → siguiente.

[8] SCOPE E HIGIENE
• Solo archivos del scope; cero refactors drive-by.
• Problema ajeno → todo.md, no código de hoy.
• Sin reestructuraciones sin [A] explícita.

[9] RECUPERACIÓN
• Main rojo heredado → revert hasta verde (nunca force).
• Conflicto → abort + pending + reporte (única pregunta permitida).
• Muerte de sesión → nada que hacer: el último checkpoint ya salvó todo;
  el funeral [2] de la próxima sesión se ocupa del cadáver.

[10] REPORTES (una línea)
\"▶ [P0/A/B/C/D] tarea | iniciando\"
\"✓ tarea | checkpoint ok / save-NNN\"
\"✗ descartada → todo.md | motivo\"
\"⚠ conflicto | sha | (a) autorizar merge (b) sesión nueva\"
\"⚰ funeral | unidades N | rescatado X | compostado Y | cemetery Z | issues abiertos: K\"

[11] CIERRE GRACIOSO
Pausa/cola vacía/auto-pacing: HANDOFF actualizado, checkpoint final, reporte
de 3 líneas: hecho / siguiente / riesgos.

[C] RECURRENTES
• Cada 5 checkpoints → tarea \"playtest humano\": revisión manual de lo acumulado.
• Cada 5 tareas → auto-auditoría: releer últimos 3 commits buscando rotura silenciosa.
• Cada 10 checkpoints → verificar que el último save-NNN siga buildeando verde
  (detecta saves falsos antes de necesitarlos).
• Si issues abiertos >2 → mini-funeral (solo 2.1→2.4, sin compost de branches).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (repetir al final):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

3: ## Estado
4: - Implementación inicial completada en una app estática de HTML/CSS/JavaScript, sin backend ni dependencias de framework.

11: - Verificación real en Chromium: demos y transporte, feedback de beatmatch, SYNC, pitch, EQ, volumen, crossfader y cue/play; biblioteca persistida y exportación JSON.

Se eligió `/tmp/opencode/djlab-test.wav` desde el botón A de esa pista y Deck A mostró `djlab-test` con duración de 1 s. El audio seleccionado fue local (URL `blob:`); no se conectó audio de YouTube al mixer.
13: - `playwright-cli console`: cero errores y advertencias en la prueba reciente. Se revisó visualmente la cabina y la lista: se mantienen los decks A/B, controles de mezcla y reproductor/lista de YouTube separados. Captura previa en `screenshots/dj-lab-final.png` (ignorada por Git).

## DJ Lab

A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.

### Run it

Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Open <http://localhost:3002>.

### Practice

- Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
- Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
- Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
- Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
- Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
- The shared playlist is embedded for playback in DJ Lab. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music. Playlist playback is separate from the DJ decks; to mix a track, load an audio file from your device.

The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

- Build a complete, playable game now, or apply the requested change to the existing game. The repository is DJ Lab, a browser-based DJ practice app; the pending feature request is its advanced analysis and library extension.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Verify with a green build and browser preview, including a small JPEG screenshot; finish work as an atomic commit and checkpoint.

## Decisions
- No new implementation decisions made. The existing app explicitly limits mixing to generated demos or user-selected local audio; YouTube playback remains separate.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read existing app documentation and inspected the DJ Lab interface and implementation.
- Fetched `origin/main` and cleanly merged it into the working branch; `origin/main` was an ancestor before the merge.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Continue with the pending advanced DJ Lab feature request: FFT/band analysis and estimated BPM, detailed beatmatch scoring, universal MIDI mapping with fader/jog, and JSON import alongside existing export.
- Establish baseline browser preview and screenshot, then implement the feature in scoped, testable increments.

### Blocked

1. Inspect the merged branch state and latest changes, then start the app and verify its current browser behavior with Playwright.
2. Decompose the advanced request into checkboxes in `todo.md` or `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`, then implement one feature slice at a time.
3. Run syntax/build checks and browser verification; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot (≤1280px wide).
4. Update relevant documentation and handoff, make an atomic commit, and attempt a fast-forward push to `main`; never force push.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: DJ decks, audio analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI, and library behavior.
- `index.html`: interface structure and control elements.
- `styles.css`: app styling and responsive layout.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

## Objective
- Implement the requested advanced analysis and library features in the existing browser-based DJ Lab, building on its current playable app.

## Requirements
- Keep analysis and mixing limited to generated demos or user-selected local audio; do not extract or proxy YouTube streams.
- Add FFT/band analysis and estimated BPM, detailed beatmatch scoring, universal MIDI mapping with fader/jog, and JSON import alongside export.
- Verify with a green build and browser preview, including a small JPEG screenshot; complete an atomic commit and checkpoint.

## Decisions
- No new implementation decisions yet; existing app keeps YouTube playback separate from the mixer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read the current handoff, README, roadmap, todo, user requests, and app code.
- Fetched and merged `origin/main` cleanly; current branch is ahead of `origin/main` by six commits and includes the latest merge.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Started the local server on port 3002 and installed the Playwright Chromium browser after preview startup initially failed because it was missing.

### Active
- Capture and inspect the baseline browser preview, then implement the advanced feature in scoped increments.

### Blocked
- GitHub issue census unavailable: `gh issue list` failed because `GH_TOKEN` is not set.
- No `save-*` tags exist.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002` with Playwright, inspect baseline behavior, and save/read a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.
2. Decompose the feature request into checkboxes in `todo.md` or `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`, then implement and verify in small slices.
3. Update documentation and handoff, run checks and browser verification, make an atomic commit, and attempt a fast-forward push to `main` without force-pushing.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: audio decks, analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI, and library behavior.
- `index.html`: interface and control elements.
- `styles.css`: app styling and responsive layout.
- `todo.md`: deferred feature request.
- `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`: feature roadmap/checklist.
- `HANDOFF.md`: implementation and verification notes.
- `README.md`: app usage and scope documentation.

## Important Context
- Current branch: `opencode/42488616157`; latest commit `edac0b5` is a clean merge of `origin/main` (`5336a3b`).
- Working tree was clean at last check; no feature implementation changes have been made.
- The local preview server is running at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright Chromium is now installed.
- `todo.md` requests local/demo-only FFT and estimated BPM, PERFECT/GOOD/DESINCRONIZADO scoring, universal MIDI mappings including fader/jog, and JSON import.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

## Objective
- Implement the advanced analysis and library features requested for the existing browser-based DJ Lab, building on its playable app.

## Requirements
- Limit audio analysis and mixing to generated demos or user-selected local audio; do not extract or proxy YouTube streams.
- Add FFT/band analysis and estimated BPM, detailed beatmatch scoring, universal MIDI mapping with fader/jog, and JSON import alongside export.
- Verify with a green build and browser preview, including a small JPEG screenshot; complete an atomic commit and checkpoint.

## Decisions
- Keep YouTube playback separate from the mixer; use only demo and local audio for analysis and mixing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Merged `origin/main` cleanly; `HEAD` is six commits ahead of `origin/main`.
- Started the local preview server on port 3002 and installed Playwright Chromium.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

## Objective
- Complete and verify DJ Lab’s audio analysis, tempo-and-phase beatmatch scoring, universal MIDI mapping, and validated JSON library import/export.
- Update documentation, capture a compact JPEG preview, commit changes atomically, and attempt a non-force push to `main`.

## Requirements
- Analyze and mix only generated demos or user-selected local audio; do not extract or proxy YouTube streams.
- Run syntax/build checks and test in Chromium; capture an updated preview.
- Update documentation and checklist; commit atomically and attempt a non-force push.

## Decisions
- Keep YouTube playback separate from the mixer; analysis and mixing are limited to demos and local audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Initial analysis readouts, FFT band calculations, and offline BPM estimation implementation.
- MIDI target selector and initial mapping persistence state.
- JSON import file control and checklist text update.
- Baseline preview captured at `screenshots/baseline.jpg`.
- Updated `checkMix()` to score tempo difference and phase difference together, regardless of playback state.

### Active
- Complete MIDI learn and mapped note/CC controls, including fader and relative jog; current `handleMidi()` still uses hard-coded mappings.
- Implement validated JSON library import; only the file control and export handler are present.
- Add styling and update `README.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `todo.md`, and `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md` to reflect verified implementation.
- Verify features in Chromium, run checks, capture updated JPEG preview, commit atomically, and attempt fast-forward push.

### Blocked
- GitHub issue census unavailable because `GH_TOKEN` is not set.

## Next Move
1. Finish MIDI learn/mapping and validated JSON import in `app.js`; check edge cases in the new tempo-and-phase scoring.
2. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`; test analysis, scoring, MIDI, and JSON import/export in Chromium.
3. Update documentation/checklist, capture a compact JPEG preview, commit atomically, and attempt a non-force push to `main`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI, and library logic.
- `index.html`: analysis readouts, MIDI mapping controls, and library import/export controls.
- `styles.css`: UI styling; new controls may need styling.
- `todo.md`: feature checklist.
- `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`: advanced-feature roadmap status.
- `README.md`: app scope and usage documentation.
- `HANDOFF.md`: implementation and verification notes.
- `screenshots/baseline.jpg`: baseline preview.

## Objective
- Complete DJ Lab’s audio analysis, tempo-and-phase beatmatch scoring, universal MIDI mapping, and validated JSON library import/export.
- Update documentation, verify in Chromium, capture a compact JPEG preview, commit atomically, and attempt a non-force push to `main`.

## Requirements
- Analyze and mix only generated demos or user-selected local audio; do not extract or proxy YouTube streams.
- Run syntax/build checks and test in Chromium; capture an updated preview.
- Update documentation and checklist; commit atomically and attempt a non-force push.

## Decisions
- Keep YouTube playback separate from the mixer; analysis and mixing are limited to demos and local audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added FFT band calculations, offline BPM estimation, and tempo-plus-wrapped-phase beatmatch scoring.
- Implemented universal MIDI learn for notes/CC, mapped transport/mixer controls, jog nudging, persisted mappings, and map reset.
- Added library track normalization/validation and JSON import/export handling; imports validate version, track shape, and limits.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Test analysis, scoring, MIDI learn/dispatch, and JSON import/export in Chromium; check console and UI.
- Update `README.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `todo.md`, and `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md` to reflect implementation and verification.
- Style/check new MIDI controls if needed; capture updated compact JPEG preview.
- Commit changes atomically and attempt a non-force push to `main`.

### Blocked
- GitHub issue census remains unavailable because `GH_TOKEN` is not set.

## Next Move
1. Start/open the app in Chromium and verify analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mappings, JSON import/export, and console output.
2. Update docs/checklist and capture the refreshed JPEG preview.
3. Re-run checks, inspect the diff, commit atomically, then attempt a non-force push to `main`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: analysis, scoring, MIDI mapping, library persistence/import/export.
- `index.html`: analysis readouts, MIDI mapping controls, and library import/export controls.
- `styles.css`: app styling; check styling for the new controls.
- `README.md`: usage and feature documentation to update.
- `HANDOFF.md`: implementation and verification notes to update.
- `todo.md`: feature checklist.
- `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`: roadmap status.
- `screenshots/baseline.jpg`: existing preview to replace/update.

## Important Context
- Current branch is `opencode/42488616157`; `HEAD` was `edac0b5`, based on `origin/main` (`5336a3b`), six commits ahead at last recorded check.
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `index.html`, `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`, and `todo.md`; `README.md` and `HANDOFF.md` remain outdated.
- Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium`; `playwright-cli` is installed. Earlier preview server was available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The latest `app.js` changes passed syntax and whitespace checks but have not yet been browser-tested.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
43: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
44: 
45: The current lesson is a first playable baseline. Detailed FFT/BPM analysis, expanded rhythm scoring and MIDI mapping, plus JSON import are deferred in `todo.md`.

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección "SOP omgithub" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final "── FIN DEL SOP ──" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: "Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

2.1 CENSO
    Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero.
    Agrupar linajes de prompts idénticos/repetidos.
    Cota forense: leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes.
    >7 días o fuera de cota → compostar SIN leer.

2.2 FORENSIS (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
    a) Tres fuentes, en orden de autoridad:
       1. Diff de código huérfano → qué hizo.
       2. HANDOFF.md del repo → qué se proponía.
       3. Thread del issue (último Work State/Next Move) → por qué murió.
       Reconciliar en UNA línea: "causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente".
    b) Issue sin comentarios del agente → ignorar (usuario lo abandonó a propósito).

2.3 COMPOST (por unidad)
    Rescate a main vía branch temporal:
       git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main
       merge checkpoints/N → si limpio y build verde:
          push FF tmp-main:main (+ tag save-NNN si es hito)
       si no: tag graveyard-checkpoints-N + mención en epitafio.
    Luego borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main, o sin código).
    Volver a tu branch; el sync [3.2] absorberá el main compostado.

2.4 SEPULTURA (mantenimiento de issues)
    Cerrar el issue con comment-epitafio:
    "⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W"
    Sin permiso para cerrar → Comment "⚰ CERRABLE: ..." y listar en reporte.

2.5 HIGIENE POST-FUNERAL
    Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máx 1 esperando humano).
    Reportar conteo final en el epitafio.

[3] BOOT
3.1 Leer: AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.
3.2 Sync preciso: HEAD ancestro de origin/main → reset --hard origin/main.
    Divergidas → merge limpio + rebuild; conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte.
3.3 Triage huérfano: si origin/main..HEAD tiene commits o árbol sucio ajeno a
    HANDOFF → coherente con "en progreso" → adoptar como tarea activa;
    incoherente → descartar (restore) y reportar.
3.4 Gate baseline: build (+tests si existen). Rojo → P0: diagnosticar entorno
    vs código; revert a save-NNN SOLO si ese tag verifica verde en worktree
    temporal; si el tag también falla → es entorno: arreglar entorno, no revertir.
3.5 Sin tags save-* → git tag save-000 && push.

[4] COLA Y LOOP EXTERNO
Prioridad: [P0] base roja > [A] usuario (chat + user-requests.md) >
[B] roadmap > [C] mantenimiento > [D] green.
Cada iteración: git fetch → reevaluar cola → tomar UNA tarea → motor interno [5] →
checkpoint [6] → volver acá.

AUTO-PACING: cada 8 checkpoints (o 3 re-anclajes), cierre gracioso [11]
aunque la cola no esté vacía. Muerte limpia > muerte infligida.

Cola vacía → HANDOFF + checkpoint final + reporte + pausa.

[5] MOTOR RALPH INTERNO (por tarea)
PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3-6 líneas en HANDOFF "en progreso".
ACT: edición mínima que cumple la tarea; solo archivos del scope.
VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea: "¿qué podría romper esto?". Si la respuesta es seria →
  agregar test o guarda antes de cerrar.
FIX: VERIFY fallido → diagnosticar → corregir → re-VERIFY (máx 3 rondas).
DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo
  commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.

Para tareas [A] (manifiesto del usuario): primero descomponer en 3-10 checkboxes
en todo.md o roadmap; luego ejecutarlas de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.

DESCARTE: 3 rondas sin éxito → revertir archivos de la tarea, todo.md con
  motivo e intentos, siguiente tarea.

[6] CHECKPOINTS
6.1 DONE con build verde → git push origin HEAD:main (fast-forward). Nunca force.
6.2 Rechazo "non-fast-forward" → fetch + merge limpio + rebuild → push;
    conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte; el loop SIGUE con [C]/[D] sin
    checkpointear reintentando el sync cada iteración; pausa total recién
    tras 3 iteraciones con el mismo conflicto.
6.3 Rechazo "403/permission" → no reintentar: reportar una vez "falta permiso
    de push a main" y seguir sin checkpoint hasta resolución humana.
6.4 Tag save-NNN solo con VERIFY aprobado (hito visible).
6.5 Todo checkpoint es punto de muerte segura.

[7] LIBROS
• HANDOFF.md: reescribir SOLO en pausa, cierre y re-anclaje (cada 5 tareas).
• todo.md: descartadas/bloqueadas con intentos (máx 3 de por vida → "requiere humano").
• user-requests.md: inbox externo; tachar al completar.
• roadmap/*.md: autogestionado con checkboxes; archivo completo → siguiente.

[8] SCOPE E HIGIENE
• Solo archivos del scope; cero refactors drive-by.
• Problema ajeno → todo.md, no código de hoy.
• Sin reestructuraciones sin [A] explícita.

[9] RECUPERACIÓN
• Main rojo heredado → revert hasta verde (nunca force).
• Conflicto → abort + pending + reporte (única pregunta permitida).
• Muerte de sesión → nada que hacer: el último checkpoint ya salvó todo;
  el funeral [2] de la próxima sesión se ocupa del cadáver.

[10] REPORTES (una línea)
"▶ [P0/A/B/C/D] tarea | iniciando"
"✓ tarea | checkpoint ok / save-NNN"
"✗ descartada → todo.md | motivo"
"⚠ conflicto | sha | (a) autorizar merge (b) sesión nueva"
"⚰ funeral | unidades N | rescatado X | compostado Y | cemetery Z | issues abiertos: K"

[11] CIERRE GRACIOSO
Pausa/cola vacía/auto-pacing: HANDOFF actualizado, checkpoint final, reporte
de 3 líneas: hecho / siguiente / riesgos.

[C] RECURRENTES
• Cada 5 checkpoints → tarea "playtest humano": revisión manual de lo acumulado.
• Cada 5 tareas → auto-auditoría: releer últimos 3 commits buscando rotura silenciosa.
• Cada 10 checkpoints → verificar que el último save-NNN siga buildeando verde
  (detecta saves falsos antes de necesitarlos).
• Si issues abiertos >2 → mini-funeral (solo 2.1→2.4, sin compost de branches).

# SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO

## Núcleo indestructible
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. Nunca force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. Nunca resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag verificado.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

## [0] Modo Ralph
- Loop de trabajo autónomo, sin preguntas aclaratorias salvo conflicto de merge.
- Asumir decisiones razonables y anotarlas en HANDOFF.md.
- Leer errores, diagnosticarlos, corregirlos y reintentar.
- No dejar tareas a medias: terminarlas o descartarlas.

## [1] Autoinstalación (solo primera vez)
- Si AGENTS.md no tiene esta sección, agregarla al final sin pisar contenido existente.
- La última línea del archivo debe ser `── FIN DEL SOP ──`. Si falta al iniciar, considerar el archivo corrupto y pedir el paste original antes de continuar.
- Crear si faltan: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md y /roadmap/.
- Repo vacío con boilerplate que exige build: esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
- Sesiones futuras arrancan con: «Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md».

## [2] Funeral, compost y mantenimiento de issues (boot)
### 2.0 Censo
Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero. Agrupar linajes de prompts repetidos. Leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes. Los de más de 7 días o fuera de cota se compostan sin leer.
### 2.1 Forensis (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
Fuentes por autoridad: (1) diff de código huérfano, qué hizo; (2) HANDOFF.md, qué se proponía; (3) thread del issue, último Work State/Next Move, por qué murió. Reconciliar en una línea: «causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente». Issue sin comentarios del agente: ignorar.

═══ SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO ═══

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección "SOP omgithub" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final "── FIN DEL SOP ──" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: "Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

2.1 CENSO
    Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero.
    Agrupar linajes de prompts idénticos/repetidos.
    Cota forense: leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes.
    >7 días o fuera de cota → compostar SIN leer.

2.2 FORENSIS (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
    a) Tres fuentes, en orden de autoridad:
       1. Diff de código huérfano → qué hizo.
       2. HANDOFF.md del repo → qué se proponía.
       3. Thread del issue (último Work State/Next Move) → por qué murió.
       Reconciliar en UNA línea: "causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente".
    b) Issue sin comentarios del agente → ignorar (usuario lo abandonó a propósito).

2.3 COMPOST (por unidad)
    Rescate a main vía branch temporal:
       git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main
       merge checkpoints/N → si limpio y build verde:
          push FF tmp-main:main (+ tag save-NNN si es hito)
       si no: tag graveyard-checkpoints-N + mención en epitafio.
    Luego borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main, o sin código).
    Volver a tu branch; el sync [3.2] absorberá el main compostado.

2.4 SEPULTURA (mantenimiento de issues)
    Cerrar el issue con comment-epitafio:
    "⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W"
    Sin permiso para cerrar → Comment "⚰ CERRABLE: ..." y listar en reporte.

2.5 HIGIENE POST-FUNERAL
    Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máx 1 esperando humano).
    Reportar conteo final en el epitafio.

[3] BOOT
3.1 Leer: AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.
3.2 Sync preciso: HEAD ancestro de origin/main → reset --hard origin/main.
    Divergidas → merge limpio + rebuild; conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte.
3.3 Triage huérfano: si origin/main..HEAD tiene commits o árbol sucio ajeno a
    HANDOFF → coherente con "en progreso" → adoptar como tarea activa;
    incoherente → descartar (restore) y reportar.
3.4 Gate baseline: build (+tests si existen). Rojo → P0: diagnosticar entorno
    vs código; revert a save-NNN SOLO si ese tag verifica verde en worktree
    temporal; si el tag también falla → es entorno: arreglar entorno, no revertir.
3.5 Sin tags save-* → git tag save-000 && push.

[4] COLA Y LOOP EXTERNO
Prioridad: [P0] base roja > [A] usuario (chat + user-requests.md) >
[B] roadmap > [C] mantenimiento > [D] green.
Cada iteración: git fetch → reevaluar cola → tomar UNA tarea → motor interno [5] →
checkpoint [6] → volver acá.

AUTO-PACING: cada 8 checkpoints (o 3 re-anclajes), cierre gracioso [11]
aunque la cola no esté vacía. Muerte limpia > muerte infligida.

Cola vacía → HANDOFF + checkpoint final + reporte + pausa.

[5] MOTOR RALPH INTERNO (por tarea)
PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3-6 líneas en HANDOFF "en progreso".
ACT: edición mínima que cumple la tarea; solo archivos del scope.
VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea: "¿qué podría romper esto?". Si la respuesta es seria →
  agregar test o guarda antes de cerrar.
FIX: VERIFY fallido → diagnosticar → corregir → re-VERIFY (máx 3 rondas).
DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo
  commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.

Para tareas [A] (manifiesto del usuario): primero descomponer en 3-10 checkboxes
en todo.md o roadmap; luego ejecutarlas de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.

DESCARTE: 3 rondas sin éxito → revertir archivos de la tarea, todo.md con
  motivo e intentos, siguiente tarea.

[6] CHECKPOINTS
6.1 DONE con build verde → git push origin HEAD:main (fast-forward). Nunca force.
6.2 Rechazo "non-fast-forward" → fetch + merge limpio + rebuild → push;
    conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte; el loop SIGUE con [C]/[D] sin
    checkpointear reintentando el sync cada iteración; pausa total recién
    tras 3 iteraciones con el mismo conflicto.
6.3 Rechazo "403/permission" → no reintentar: reportar una vez "falta permiso
    de push a main" y seguir sin checkpoint hasta resolución humana.
6.4 Tag save-NNN solo con VERIFY aprobado (hito visible).
6.5 Todo checkpoint es punto de muerte segura.

[7] LIBROS
• HANDOFF.md: reescribir SOLO en pausa, cierre y re-anclaje (cada 5 tareas).
• todo.md: descartadas/bloqueadas con intentos (máx 3 de por vida → "requiere humano").
• user-requests.md: inbox externo; tachar al completar.
• roadmap/*.md: autogestionado con checkboxes; archivo completo → siguiente.

[8] SCOPE E HIGIENE
• Solo archivos del scope; cero refactors drive-by.
• Problema ajeno → todo.md, no código de hoy.
• Sin reestructuraciones sin [A] explícita.

[9] RECUPERACIÓN
• Main rojo heredado → revert hasta verde (nunca force).
• Conflicto → abort + pending + reporte (única pregunta permitida).
• Muerte de sesión → nada que hacer: el último checkpoint ya salvó todo;
  el funeral [2] de la próxima sesión se ocupa del cadáver.

[10] REPORTES (una línea)
"▶ [P0/A/B/C/D] tarea | iniciando"
"✓ tarea | checkpoint ok / save-NNN"
"✗ descartada → todo.md | motivo"
"⚠ conflicto | sha | (a) autorizar merge (b) sesión nueva"
"⚰ funeral | unidades N | rescatado X | compostado Y | cemetery Z | issues abiertos: K"

[11] CIERRE GRACIOSO
Pausa/cola vacía/auto-pacing: HANDOFF actualizado, checkpoint final, reporte
de 3 líneas: hecho / siguiente / riesgos.

[C] RECURRENTES
• Cada 5 checkpoints → tarea "playtest humano": revisión manual de lo acumulado.
• Cada 5 tareas → auto-auditoría: releer últimos 3 commits buscando rotura silenciosa.
• Cada 10 checkpoints → verificar que el último save-NNN siga buildeando verde
  (detecta saves falsos antes de necesitarlos).
• Si issues abiertos >2 → mini-funeral (solo 2.1→2.4, sin compost de branches).

2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.

4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

47: ## [5] Motor Ralph interno (por tarea)
48: - PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3–6 líneas en HANDOFF «en progreso».
49: - ACT: edición mínima, solo archivos del scope.
50: - VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
51: - AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea «¿qué podría romper esto?». Si es serio, agregar test o guarda.
52: - FIX: si VERIFY falla, diagnosticar, corregir y re-verificar (máximo 3 rondas).
53: - DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.
54: - Para tareas [A], descomponer el manifiesto en 3–10 checkboxes en todo.md o roadmap y ejecutar de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.
55: - DESCARTE: tras 3 rondas sin éxito, revertir archivos de la tarea, anotar motivo e intentos en todo.md (máximo 3 de por vida → «requiere humano») y seguir.
56: 
57: ## [6] Checkpoints
58: 1. DONE con build verde → `git push origin HEAD:main` (fast-forward; nunca force).
59: 2. Rechazo non-fast-forward: fetch + merge limpio + rebuild + push. Conflicto: abort + pending-N + reporte; seguir [C]/[D] sin reintentar el sync cada iteración; pausar tras 3 iteraciones con el mismo conflicto.
60: 3. Rechazo 403/permission: no reintentar; reportar una vez «falta permiso de push a main» y seguir sin checkpoint hasta resolución humana.
61: 4. Tag save-NNN solo con VERIFY aprobado (hito visible).
62: 5. Todo checkpoint es punto de muerte segura.
63: 
64: ## [7] Libros
65: - HANDOFF.md: reescribir solo en pausa, cierre y re-anclaje (cada 5 tareas).
66: - todo.md: descartadas/bloqueadas con intentos (máximo 3 de por vida → «requiere humano»).
67: - user-requests.md: inbox externo; tachar al completar.
68: - roadmap/*.md: autogestionado con checkboxes; archivo completo → siguiente.
69: 
70: ## [8] Scope e higiene
71: Solo archivos del scope; cero refactors drive-by. Problema ajeno → todo.md, no código de hoy. Sin reestructuraciones sin [A] explícita.
72: 
73: ## [9] Recuperación
74: - Main rojo heredado → revert hasta verde (nunca force).
75: - Conflicto → abort + pending + reporte (única pregunta permitida).
76: - Muerte de sesión: el último checkpoint ya salvó todo; el funeral [2] de la próxima sesión atiende el cadáver.
77: 
78: ## [10] Reportes (una línea)
79: - `▶ [P0/A/B/C/D] tarea | iniciando`
80: - `✓ tarea | checkpoint ok / save-NNN`
81: - `✗ descartada → todo.md | motivo`
82: - `⚠ conflicto | sha | (a) autorizar merge (b) sesión nueva`
83: - `⚰ funeral | unidades N | rescatado X | compostado Y | cemetery Z | issues abiertos: K`
84: 
85: ## [11] Cierre gracioso
86: En pausa/cola vacía/auto-pacing: HANDOFF actualizado, checkpoint final, reporte de 3 líneas: hecho / siguiente / riesgos.
87: 
88: ## [C] Recurrentes
89: - Cada 5 checkpoints: tarea «playtest humano», revisión manual de lo acumulado.
90: - Cada 5 tareas: auto-auditoría, releer últimos 3 commits buscando rotura silenciosa.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for beatmatch feedback based on tempo difference and wrapped beat phase. Local/demo playback also shows live low/mid/high frequency levels and an offline BPM estimate; YouTube audio is never analyzed or routed into the mixer.
41: - The MIDI panel supports universal learn for note and CC messages across transport, mixer controls, and relative jog nudging. Assignments are saved in this browser and can be reset; WebMIDI availability depends on the browser and device.
42: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads versioned JSON metadata and **IMPORTAR** validates compatible files (up to 100 tracks/1 MB); audio files themselves are never included, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
43: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
44: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
45: 
46: The current lesson is a playable browser-only baseline. The completed analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mapping, and validated library import/export checklist is in `todo.md`.

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección "SOP omgithub" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final "── FIN DEL SOP ──" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: "Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for beatmatch feedback based on tempo difference and wrapped beat phase. Local/demo playback also shows live low/mid/high frequency levels and an offline BPM estimate; YouTube audio is never analyzed or routed into the mixer.
41: - The MIDI panel supports universal learn for note and CC messages across transport, mixer controls, and relative jog nudging. Assignments are saved in this browser and can be reset; WebMIDI availability depends on the browser and device.
42: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads versioned JSON metadata and **IMPORTAR** validates compatible files (up to 100 tracks/1 MB); audio files themselves are never included, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
43: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
44: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. A/B on those rows opens a local file picker and loads only the file you choose. YouTube playback stays separate and is never routed into the mixer. If YouTube does not allow embedding a track, open the playlist in YouTube Music.
45: 
46: The current lesson is a playable browser-only baseline. The completed analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mapping, and validated library import/export checklist is in `todo.md`.
